handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 65r, 65v was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 68 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 68 original annotation rows for 68 distinct source verses, with no duplicate selection needed. Every original rectangle was inspected and contains its corresponding verse; all original bounds are retained. Some rectangles include neighbouring text, and marginal additions may fall outside the navigation rectangle. sourceWitness=LL and panelId are annotation provenance only; no LL text was consulted.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Full-page inspection of folios 65r and 65v shows alternate physical verse lines inset; rend="indent" records that visible layout on even verses. The lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: A different agent independently read all 68 source verses and investigated every evidence note. Source-supported corrections and interventions were made directly. Residual uncertainty concerns source letters or mark function and remains documented without human-review assignments. The hash-bound review ledger records per-note dispositions; independent review does not confer human scholarly approval.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 68 verses and visible interventions in folios 65r, 65v; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

Independently checked all 68 verses, both full-page layouts and all 43 first-pass notes. Corrected 16 to tentative rupit and 23 to altis; encoded two expunction substitutions at 24, the insertion caret at 26, and the cancelled extra e at 53. Original zone coordinates and source-supported insets remain unchanged. Documented uncertainty retained; zero human escalations.

div.head: Source evidence after independent review
div.note: An enlarged ornamental M opens the poem. The source repeats mater in Memnona si mater mater; both are retained. The u of plorauit is dark.
A slender vertical stroke crosses the space after Et. Its function is uncertain; it is retained schematically as a metamark, not a letter.
The initial e of elegia has a darker disturbed area. It is retained as unclear without reconstructing an earlier spelling or asserting erasure.

The baseline starts A nimis. A small raised h-like shape appears beside the A and is encoded as an uncertain addition. No letter is silently supplied in the baseline. An x-like right-margin mark at this level has unspecified function and is documented here.
The source has uersāq, without an initial e. The bar over a and suspended q are explicitly expanded uersamque. The e of fert and barred a are darker.
A slender vertical stroke occurs between sparsi and per. Its function is unknown; a schematic metamark records its presence without adding a letter.
The visible phrase reads in aeneae. The name is preserved without normalization.
Egressum tectis is read with editorial word separation. The source name iule is retained.

The u-region of iuueni is darker. Independent enlargement supports rupit rather than the first-pass ruptum: no separate um sequence is visible, but the close-set i/t remains qualified. The uncertain reading stays local; no normalized text supplies an unseen ending.
The ending men of numen has dark overlapping strokes. Current numen is tentative locally; no erased reading or hand is reconstructed. The et ligature forms the beginning of etiam.
The et ligature closes Scilicet. Omn in omne is darker. The current wording is retained without inferring a deleted alternative.
The final long s of obscuras is dark; no earlier letter is supplied.

Patris is crossed by crowded strokes, so its current reading remains unclear rather than declaring a complete cancellation. Maro follows, with a slender vertical mark before quid. The source phrase is not normalized to a familiar reading.
A small u is added above the i-region of obstipuisse. Both the baseline and raised letter are retained; no cancellation of baseline i is asserted. A question-like sign ends the verse.

Independent enlargement reads main-line elinon altis, with et written above the initial e. Altis has no separate e after l; the first-pass aletis was corrected. Baseline and addition remain separately encoded without silently deleting the baseline e.

Independent enlarged crops show expunction dots below both in lyra and comam, with inuicta above the former and lyra above the latter. These two replacements are encoded as subst, retaining each cancelled baseline phrase and its raised addition. No historical correcting hand is assigned.
Final n of maeoniden, the following a, and ceu are darker. These current readings are retained without reconstructing previous letters.

The baseline has periis, with a small i above after p and a small caret beneath the insertion area. Both the addition and the below-line insertion metamark are now encoded, preserving the original components separately.
The et ending of Duret is a dark ligature. The final us of opus and initial f of fama are also darker; no erasure is inferred.
The visible place-related form is egypta. No i or other normalization is supplied.
A dark s stands above the l/o interval of main-line falo. The insertion is retained as add, without pretending the s is written on the baseline.
Colon-like marks follow both occurrences of pius. Small oblique marginal strokes beside the verse are documented without assigning them a correction function.
The initial V and separate e are dark. The urna area is pale and disturbed between r and n. Current urna is qualified; no missing earlier letter or erasure history is inferred.
The line ends with a question-like sign, preserved schematically.
A question-like sign also closes this line; no modern punctuation is supplied.
The source writes sanctorum in full. It is not replaced with a familiar alternate adjective.
The final a of pheacia and u of tellus are darker. Source Sed is written with separate letters here, not an et ligature.
The source ending has a dark o in humo followed by a brown m crossed horizontally. The cancelled m is retained as del; the preceding dark o is recorded without reconstructing an earlier state.

Hic is written above the initial Hinc. Black dots beneath madidos indicate expunction and abbreviated manib with a terminal us sign is written above it. Both layers are encoded as a substitution, with explicit manibus expansion.
An et ligature is added above the space between Mater and in, with a small caret below. Both the raised addition and insertion mark are retained.
A small h-like group is written above the initial H of Hinc. The exact letters are uncertain and remain in unclear within add; the baseline word is unchanged.

Independent enlargement reveals a baseline e between n and x in iunexerunt, with a clear black expunction dot directly below and a dark stroke within the e. The cancelled letter is restored in del rend=expunction; the resulting reading is iunxerunt. No erased predecessor or historical hand is invented.

A dot below the first e of descendens and i above it support an expunction/replacement. Likewise, final s of inquis has a dot beneath and t above. Both substitutions retain their original and replacement letters.

The final s of ais is dark. A faint left-margin inscription at approximately verses57–58 appears quod; it is retained as unclear at the nearest verse, without claiming an exact attachment or expansion. The source line ends doloris, not a normalized dative.
The initial M is darker. A question-like sign ends the line.
The opening is S followed by tamen. No separate i is visible and none is silently supplied. The et ligature before umbra is retained.
A slender vertical stroke follows Restat. It is recorded schematically with unspecified function, not read as a letter.
A slender stroke follows Tempora. The second l-region of catulle is dark. No earlier reading is inferred from these marks.

The opening Sanguis carries a suspension bar over the ui-region; Sanguinis is an explicit tentative expansion. The ending of prodige is heavily dark and overlapped, remaining locally unclear; final e of galle is dark. Three parallel right-margin strokes at this level have unspecified function.
The source opening reads His comes. After siqua, a dark barred e is explicitly expanded est. The earlier tua est is separated editorially.
Tuos is written above pios. The main word remains visible and is not declared cancelled.
A vertical stroke crosses the tuta/requiescite boundary. It is retained as an unspecified metamark; no cancellation of the phrase is asserted.

Humus is a dark hum with terminal us sign and has an explicit expansion. Initial t of tuo is darker. A terminal colon-like mark and long stroke separate the poem from the large A beginning3.10 below. That next verse is not a heading.
